name: Left communism
summary: Left communism is the revolutionary-Marxist current that broke with the Third International over parliamentary participation, trade-union work, alliances with other parties and national liberation. It holds that the working class must make revolution through its own mass organs, that the Soviet system became state capitalism, and that wage labour and money must be abolished. Its Italian and Dutch-German strands differ chiefly over the role of the party versus workers' councils.
scope: The communist left as a family: the Italian current (Bordiga, Damen; Lyons Theses 1926) and the Dutch-German council-communist current (Gorter, Pannekoek; KAPD), plus the later ICC tradition as described in Wikipedia. Excludes Trotskyism, Marxism-Leninism, and later communization theory. Where strands split (party, unions, centralism), answers are 0 or low confidence.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Production for profit through markets is the system left communists want overthrown, replaced by conscious planning free of competition's waste and crises.

public-ownership.rationale: Pannekoek says state ownership only swaps capitalists for a bureaucracy, so left communists reject nationalisation as socialism while also opposing private ownership.

unions-good.rationale: Council communists and Gorter call the unions bureaucratic and counter-revolutionary, while Bordigists work inside them, so the current is split.

property-fundamental.rationale: Abolition of private ownership of the means of production is a core communist aim.

worker-ownership.rationale: Workers' management through councils is central, but left communists favour society-wide common ownership over ownership by each firm, so the answer is mixed.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The tradition has no settled position on drug policy; adherents are split or indifferent.

strong-leader.rationale: Gorter and Pannekoek stress that the masses must act for themselves and that leader-driven tactics fail; workers cannot be freed by others.

state-harmful.rationale: Left communists aim at ending state power and reject the anarchist denial of a transitional proletarian state, so they agree the state is ultimately unnecessary but not that it should be abolished at once.

empower-police-military.rationale: Police and army are instruments of ruling-class power, and left communists oppose strengthening them.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: No settled position; some see sex work as commodification under capitalism, others support decriminalisation.

decide-locally.rationale: Council communism has a bottom-up federal structure, but Italian currents stress centralism; split.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Left communists see racial divisions as dividing the working class and reject identity-based programmes, yet oppose racism; split on remedy.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Left communists oppose nationalism and see the proletariat as an international class.

gradual-change.rationale: They reject reformism and parliamentary gradualism in favour of revolution led by the workers' own struggle.

free-trade.rationale: Capitalist trade is a form of exploitation that left communists reject; they do not treat it as benefiting all.

nation-first.rationale: Both main currents oppose nationalism and favour international working-class solidarity.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Interventions are viewed as imperialist wars; left communists back no side in imperialist conflicts.

open-borders.rationale: Communism abolishes nations and borders; left communists reject nationalism and see the working class as international.

limit-growth.rationale: Not directly addressed; Marxist view is that capitalist accumulation is the problem, not growth as such, and abolishing it permits planning.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Left communists see climate crisis as caused by capitalism but doubt that bourgeois governments can act; they reject state action as a solution.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Marxist view holds technology serves capital within capitalism; solutions need social transformation.

revolution-justified.rationale: Revolution by the working class is the core of the tradition, as in Pannekoek's account of revolution as the workers' self-liberation.

experts-over-public.rationale: Pannekoek says decisions are made by the workers themselves, not experts or a central authority.

central-planning.rationale: They favour conscious planned production, but reject state-run planning by a bureaucracy; Pannekoek calls bureaucratic planning state capitalism, so agreement is qualified.

socialized-markets.rationale: Left communists want to abolish commodity production and money, not have market socialism.

land-value-tax.rationale: A tax scheme preserving the market and private land ownership is incompatible with their goals.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Protectionism is a national capitalist policy; left communists oppose nationalism.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State capitalism is criticised by left communists as the Soviet model.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The goal is the abolition of private property, not its wider spread.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about abolishing wage labour, not money, and the statement now asks only about money; wage labour has its own statement.

reviewHistory.rationale: Pannekoek describes labour measured directly in hours rather than value, and left communism aims at abolishing wage labour.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about abolishing wage labour, not money, and the statement now asks only about money; wage labour has its own statement.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The market-based aim is alien; they want money abolished, not left to the market. Agreement on abolition is only superficial.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised class collaboration contradicts class struggle and independent workers' organisation.

one-party-rule.rationale: Dutch-German current rejects party rule for councils, while Bordigists favour the party's leading role; the mainstream view opposes party-state power. Contested.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Opposed on communist principles to hereditary rule.

democracy-best.rationale: Left communists reject bourgeois parliamentary democracy and Lyons theses treat formal democracy as only an occasionally useful practice.

workers-councils.rationale: Pannekoek and the Dutch-German current make councils the basis of power.

right-to-secede.rationale: The tradition rejects national self-determination but opposes forced union; no settled view.

natural-rulers.rationale: Opposed to hierarchy and rule of any class; the working class governs itself.

war-builds-character.rationale: They regard war as an imperialist capitalist enterprise and call for working people to oppose it.

military-superiority.rationale: Nationalist military rivalry is imperialist; left communists oppose it.

ethnic-nation.rationale: They oppose nationalism and favour an international working class.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The classic Marxist thesis, central to left communism.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Communism aims at classless distribution by need; yet the transitional phase ties consumption to work, so not wholly stated.

civilizational-union.rationale: Religion or civilization-based blocs are nationalist/imperialist and contradict class internationalism.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Capitalism, not industry as such, is blamed; Pannekoek expects planned industrial production.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Decisions should be made by workers in assemblies, not experts or central authorities.

restore-past-order.rationale: The tradition is forward-looking and revolutionary.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Left communists hold firmly to principles over opportunist compromise, as Gorter criticises opportunism.

direct-action.rationale: Gorter rejects parliament and says workers must liberate themselves; left communists favour mass action outside elections.

means-match-ends.rationale: Gorter and Pannekoek insist workers' self-organisation in the struggle prefigures the new society; reject parliament and leader-driven tactics.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Left communists look to planned industrial production for need under workers' control (Pannekoek), not a return to foraging.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Communist principle of distribution by need, with an initial period of work-based accounting.

production-for-use.rationale: Pannekoek says aim shifts from profit to providing life necessities.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Pannekoek and the communist left follow Marx in holding that profit is surplus labour taken from the workers who produce it.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Lyons Theses call for it, and Gorter mentions dictatorship of the masses; the Dutch-German current frames it as council power rather than party rule.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Left communism originated in opposition to the First World War and imperialist wars.

taxation-theft.rationale: Taxation is a function of the state; left communists see the state as a class instrument to be overthrown, not as a thief of private property rights.

conscription.rationale: Imperialist armies are opposed; left communists back no side in imperialist wars.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The freedom to exit a state as a check on power belongs to market-liberal thought, whereas left communists place the check in workers' collective control through councils.

state-as-business.rationale: Running the state as a business would extend the market logic that left communists want to abolish; they want production organised for need.

media-academia-power.rationale: They see the capitalist class and its state as the holders of power.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation through corporate bodies fuses class interests, against the independent class organisation and council delegation left communists favour.

total-state.rationale: They reject state capitalism and call for the workers' self-rule.

national-rebirth.rationale: National regeneration is a nationalist project; both main left-communist currents reject nationalism in favour of the international working class.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Territorial expansion is a feature of imperialism, which left communists treat as inseparable from capitalism and oppose.

single-common-good.rationale: Politics is class struggle rather than a single common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Left communists oppose nationalism and national liberation movements.

revive-national-language.rationale: Reviving a national language as a state language is part of nation-building, which left communists oppose along with national liberation movements.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Workers' self-management is central, though they want it society-wide.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy within capitalism is not a left-communist concern, as they seek its overthrow, so there is no meaningful position.

economic-freedom.rationale: Left communists deny that market freedom is the basis of political freedom; Pannekoek says even state-owned production leaves workers subordinate unless they control it.

national-self-determination.rationale: Both currents oppose national liberation movements.

force-without-un.rationale: Left communists back no side in imperialist conflicts, and the UN is itself seen as an arena of the powers; so unilateral force is not supported either.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Workers are an international class, so welfare discrimination by citizenship is rejected.

class-collaboration.rationale: Left communists reject collaboration; Gorter says compromise is pointless and harmful.

dominated-front.rationale: Opposes national liberation fronts and anti-imperialist blocs.

workers-nation.rationale: They hold the working class is an international class.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Core Marxist view held by left communists, and Lyons Theses treat the state as class domination.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: National culture is not a value in the tradition.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy theory incompatible with class analysis.

proportional-representation.rationale: They reject parliament altogether, so electoral design does not matter.

national-mission.rationale: A national mission to spread a form of government is imperialist in the left-communist view and conflicts with their opposition to nationalism.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: They see parties and officials as not accountable delegates, per Pannekoek.

night-watchman-state.rationale: A state limited to defending property is the bourgeois state that left communists seek to overthrow, since they hold it protects the ruling class.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Universal equality is a communist aim, though they critique bourgeois legal equality.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Left communists reject socialism in one country; revolution must be international.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The state is class domination, and they criticise Soviet state capitalism.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Revolution and dictatorship against the ruling class involve force.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Left communists see competition under capitalism as producing waste, crisis and unemployment, which planned production would remove (Pannekoek).

separated-powers.rationale: They reject bourgeois constitutional forms in favour of councils.

vanguard-party.rationale: The Italian current insists on a disciplined party as leader, while Dutch-German current rejects party leadership, so adherents are split.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Left communism puts the working class as the revolutionary subject, not a priority-for-the-poor principle, and addresses neither directly.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Left communists see strikes as a vital means of workers' struggle (Gorter backs shop-floor organisation), so legal restrictions are opposed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Opposed; Marxist view holds poverty comes from social institutions.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Dutch-German current rejects party control, workers decide.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Bordigists favour organic centralism, while council communists reject centralism; split.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Left communism originated in opposition to imperialist war and rejects support for either camp.

recall-officials.rationale: Council delegates carry mandates and return for new mandates per Pannekoek.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: They oppose imperialist blocs but seek the end of states altogether.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reunification is a nationalist aim; both left-communist strands oppose nationalism and national liberation.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Descent-based citizenship entrenches national and ethnic divisions that left communists reject.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill-style nonconformity is not a left-communist theme; adherents are indifferent.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Candidate; anti-imperialism but they reject national liberation; no stated view.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Candidate; they oppose national liberation and see independence as irrelevant to class struggle.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Candidate; they reject parliamentarism and elected assemblies.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Candidate; opposed to Soviet state capitalist development.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Candidate; state aid is a bourgeois instrument.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Candidate; opposed to nationalism and military rivalry.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Candidate; opposed to bourgeois electoral institutions.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Left communists of both strands, and Pannekoek on bureaucratic state ownership, treat Soviet industry as state capitalism.

collective-defense.rationale: Left communists oppose alliances and imperialist wars and want workers to turn them into class war, so they reject treating an attack on an ally as obliging all.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Left communists reject national self-determination and treat borders as capitalist, so they do not frame annexation as unlawful occupation; no settled line.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: They want religion to wither and oppose the state itself, so they do not favour state curbing of churches; adherents split between hostility to the Church and hostility to the state.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale rests on general self-government, separate laws or no stated position, not on keeping a distinct economic system, and the statement now asks only whether a region joining a larger state should be free to keep its economic system.

reviewHistory.rationale: Council communists favour federated autonomous councils while rejecting any state, so the statement does not map cleanly.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale rests on general self-government, separate laws or no stated position, not on keeping a distinct economic system, and the statement now asks only whether a region joining a larger state should be free to keep its economic system.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Marxist materialism and opposition to rulers rule out a sacred, divinely descended head of state.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marxist materialism holds that social conditions shape people, and Pannekoek argues that workers change themselves through the struggle and councils.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: They oppose any ruler standing above the working class; power belongs to councils and the party is not above the class.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Council communists want power to rest wholly with the workers' councils, not shared with any elite or mixed body.

leader-cult.rationale: Gorter and Pannekoek attacked leader-centred bureaucracy and the Soviet cult around Lenin and Stalin; mass self-action is the principle.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Left communists hold the USSR became state capitalism run by a new bureaucratic class.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: They reject nationalism and national-liberation struggles in favour of class internationalism.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism is the Marxist core that left communists share.

no-bailouts.rationale: They oppose capital but reject reformist state programmes; no defined line.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: They stress mass self-action by the working class and reject minority putschism.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Left communists oppose colonialism and imperialism as capitalist domination and reject any bourgeois civilising mission.

patriotic-education.rationale: Their internationalism holds that workers have no fatherland, so teaching national loyalty serves the bourgeoisie.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Marxist crisis theory, held firmly by Bordigists and the ICC, says capitalism faces recurring and eventually terminal crisis.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Left communists reject parliament as a bourgeois institution and want workers' councils, not parliament, to hold power.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Left communists demand active revolutionary participation by the working class in its own councils, rejecting passivity.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Left communists, like Marxists generally, hold that bourgeois culture and media shape workers' thinking and reproduce capitalism; Pannekoek discusses ideological domination.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Pannekoek and Gorter hold that the bourgeoisie rules through ideology, the press and unions as well as by force; the consent theory is Gramscian but compatible.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Left communists hold imperialism extracts surplus from poorer regions, though they reject national liberation as a remedy.

native-born-offices.rationale: Left communists are internationalist and reject national distinctions among workers.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Left communists reject national claims and nationalism as bourgeois, so demanding territory is rejected.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Left communists reject national liberation and identity-based politics, holding class as the only basis for political power.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Left communists hold that the army is an arm of the capitalist state that must be destroyed and replaced by armed workers.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Workers' councils are built on delegates who are mandated and recallable by those who chose them.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Gorter rejects parliamentary action, so parliamentary budget approval is not a left-communist demand.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The ICC and other left communists reject taking sides in national struggles as part of inter-imperialist conflict.

corporate-influence.rationale: The state is seen as the committee of the capitalist class, so capital's sway over government is structural rather than a scandal.

democratic-peace.rationale: Left communists treat parliamentary democracy as a bourgeois form and wars as products of capitalist rivalry, not regime type.

industrial-unions.rationale: Strands split: council communists favoured industrial unions at first, while the Italian left and ICC reject unions as integrated into capital.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Marxist class analysis explains social conflict by class, not by hidden ethnic or religious plots.

informal-organisation.rationale: Council communists want mass organs but reject permanent parties; the Italian left insists on a party, so the strands split.

religious-nation.rationale: Left communism is internationalist and materialist; nation by religion is foreign to it.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Pannekoek's labour-accounting model leaves personal consumption private while production is held in common.

defeat-communism.rationale: Left communists are communists; they oppose the capitalist order and claim to be its revolutionary opponents.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The Marxist tradition holds capitalism built the productive base for communism, though the left holds its progressive phase is over.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: They call the USSR state capitalism and seek communism, so a third course is rejected.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Council communists want independent workers' organs and condemned Soviet repression, while the Italian current's Lyons Theses endorse the dictatorship of the proletariat suppressing bourgeois opposition, so the current is split.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: As an internationalist current opposed to imperialism and capital, it rejects governing territories for a ruling country's economic gain, though it also rejected national-liberation alliances.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Council communists hold that workers must decide directly through councils in workplaces and communities, a core tenet of the current.

alienated-labor.rationale: Its programme is to abolish wage labour and money, which presumes that labour under capital is alienated.

social-market-economy.rationale: It aims to abolish wage labour and money, so it rejects both laissez-faire and managed market capitalism.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: It rejected alliances with other parties and opposed both imperialist camps in war, so staying out of rival blocs is its position.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Left communists reject national programmes and reformist demands, but also oppose imperialism and its financial instruments; no settled line.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Not a theme of the classical left-communist texts; later currents differ and the sources are silent.

reification.rationale: Pannekoek and the Marxist tradition hold that under capitalism production is ruled by blind economic forces that escape human control, which is the substance of reification.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The Lyons Theses and Gorter treat formal democratic freedoms as bourgeois, since capitalist ownership decides who can actually be heard.

racial-franchise.rationale: Left communists are internationalist and reject national liberation and any ethnic basis for political rights.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Uniformed national-service youth movements run against the internationalism and the self-organisation of workers that left communists hold central.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Production for need with labour accounting and abolition of wage labour and class ownership means income tied to work, not property, as Pannekoek describes.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Marxism treats nations as historical products of capitalism, and left communists reject national liberation and national identity as a basis of politics.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Left communists do not address the sex/gender debate; later communisation currents differ, so adherents are split or indifferent.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Honouring national martyrs is nationalism that left communists reject; the proletarian is a class fighter, not a martyr of the nation.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Historical materialism is atheist and materialist and explains politics by class conflict, not a spiritual contest of good and evil.

culture-before-state.rationale: Nationalist cultural renewal is rejected, and left communists hold the state to be an instrument of class rule to be destroyed, not built.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Rule by a national majority over minorities contradicts proletarian internationalism and class unity across nationalities.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Rejects national self-determination and national liberation as bourgeois, so merging regions along ethnic lines is not supported.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Pannekoek holds that state ownership without council power is state capitalism, not socialism.

second-chamber.rationale: Power is vested in workers' councils; a second chamber is alien to council democracy.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Council communists favour federated councils with recallable delegates but the Italian strand stresses the centralised party; split.

family-wage.rationale: Left communists aim to abolish wage labour and money, so a wage level for a family is not the aim.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Left communists reject national liberation and cross-class alliances; class, not race, is the basis of politics.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Left communists reject defending the nation in imperialist wars and national liberation struggles, so defence-only armed forces is not their position.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Left communists reject national identity as a basis for politics and hold that class, not language or history, defines the political subject.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The family is critical of trade-union work as integrated into capital, so union bargaining is not its programme.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The current treats budget policy as an internal matter of capitalism and is indifferent to such rules.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Left communists reject national liberation and reform of the capitalist order, so reordering world trade rules is not their aim.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Pannekoek and the family hold that workers' councils must replace the state rather than inherit it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The current aims at one communist goal, abolishing wage labour and money, so a plurality of economic systems is not its view.

sacred-nation.rationale: Left communism is internationalist and rejects nationalism and national liberation struggles.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The current rejects national-liberation framings and analyses exploitation by class rather than by region.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Italian current insists on a party, while the council-communist current rejects party forms, so the family is split.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Left communists reject bourgeois parliamentary democracy as a cover for class rule and hold that real democracy means workers' councils, not elections.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Left communists want wage labour and money abolished, so a cash payment that patches capitalism is reformist, not the aim.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Left communists want private ownership abolished and production run for need by the community, so first-come private claims to resources run against this.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Both strands call the Soviet state state capitalism, so a bureaucratically ruled state economy is not worth defending.

indirect-election.rationale: Council communism has delegates chosen by and recallable to lower councils; Pannekoek makes the council system central.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Left communists reject nationalism and hold that workers have no fatherland; a spiritual duty to defend ancestral land contradicts their internationalism.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Left communism rejects national liberation and national solidarity as bourgeois, so protecting co-nationals abroad as a state aim is opposed.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Left communists reject the party bypassing the class: the Italian strand holds the party guides the class, while council communists want workers' councils, so a leader-centred bypass is opposed.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Left communism rejects nationalism and tradition in favour of a new classless society, so a return to ancestral values is opposed.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Left communists hold that a distribution is shaped by the class relations of production, and they seek to abolish wage labour and private appropriation, so voluntary exchange does not make a fortune fair.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Abolishing wage labour and reducing necessary labour time is central to the communist aim, so automation under workers' control to cut work is endorsed.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Pannekoek and Bordiga work within Marx's analysis, in which value is created by labour and surplus value is extracted from it.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Left communists reject national liberation and patriotic alliances and hold that workers have no fatherland, as in the Open Letter to Lenin.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Left communists hold that the Soviet and Chinese party-led systems with markets were state capitalism, and that the party must not rule over the class or run a market economy.

police-more-powers.rationale: Police and army are instruments of ruling-class power, and left communists oppose strengthening them. (Moved from empower-police-military, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about military spending alone.)

missingStatements.text: The Soviet Union was a state-capitalist society, not a socialist one.
missingStatements.rationale: Left communists of both strands, and Pannekoek on bureaucratic state ownership, treat Soviet industry as state capitalism.

missingStatements.text: Revolutionaries should refuse to take part in parliamentary elections.
missingStatements.rationale: Gorter rejects parliamentary action as handing the struggle to representatives, and the ICC and Bordigists oppose it.

missingStatements.text: Revolutionary parties should not form alliances or united fronts with reformist parties.
missingStatements.rationale: Gorter calls compromise and alliances pointless, and the Lyons Theses reject the workers' government slogan.
missingStatements.declined: Tactical question about united fronts, specific to Leninist and left-communist debates and too narrow for the bank.

notes: Strands diverge: Italians favour a leading party and 'organic centralism', Dutch-German council communists reject party leadership. Source rationales marked low are inferred. Not all positions verified in primary texts; ICC details rest on Wikipedia.
